summary: Pelasgus (Ancient Greek: Πελασγός) of Larissa is, in Apollodorus' Trojan-ally stemma, the father of Hippothous, co-captain of the Pelasgian contingent. Homer instead names Hippothous and Pylaeus sons of Pelasgian Lethus son of Teutamides — a parentage fork the atlas records without collapsing the two lines. He is distinct from the Arcadian autochthon and other regional Pelasgus founders.

sections.heading: Homeric Pelasgian house
paragraphs: Apollodorus lists a Pelasgus as father of Hippothous among the Trojan leaders who fight with the Dardanians and other allies. Homer's Catalogue of Ships instead makes Hippothous and Pylaeus sons of Lethus the Pelasgian, son of Teutamides, captains of the spear-raging Pelasgi from deep-soiled Larisa.

Some notices treat the Homeric father as belonging to the wider Thessalian Pelasgian stem that leads through Teutamides; the atlas id pelasgus-larissa is the Larissan house-father of Hippothous alone, not the Arcadian or Argive founder-kings of the same name.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (pelasgus-larissa) must not be merged with pelasgus-arcadia (the Arcadian autochthon and father of Lycaon), with Inachid Argive Pelasgi, or with the Thessalian son of Poseidon and Larissa. His son is hippothous-pelasgian; Pylaeus remains pylaeus-pelasgian.
